Let me analyze this OIML certificate document.

Certificate details:
- Number: R85/1998-NL1-07.03
- Member state: The Netherlands
- Project number: 511252
- Page total: 2
- Date issued: 11 October 2007 (2007-10-11)
- Issuing authority: NMi Certin B.V., Hugo de Grootplein 1, 3314 EG Dordrecht, The Netherlands
- Person responsible: Ing. C. Oosterman, Manager Product Certification
- Phone: +31 78 6332332
- Email: certin@nmi.nl
- Website: www.nmi.nl
- OIML issuer ID: NMi Certin... The certificate says "The notification of NMi Certin as Issuing Authority can be verified at www.oiml.org." There's no explicit issuer ID number. Omit.

Applicant: Enraf B.V., Delftechpark 39, 2628 XJ Delft, The Netherlands
Manufacturer: Enraf B.V., same address.

Certified type:
- Category: "Automatic level gauge" (for measuring the level of liquid in storage tanks). R85 is "Automatic level gauges for tanks" — could be category "Automatic level gauge" or "Level gauge".
- Type designations: model Smartradar Flexline, type XP. Also antennas F08, W06, H04, S06, S08, S10, S12.
- Description: "Automatic level gauge for measuring the level of liquid in storage tanks, model Smartradar Flexline, type XP, with the antennas F08, W06, H04, S06, S08, S10 and S12."

Model family: The cert covers variants by antenna type. The antennas are configurations/variants: F08, W06, H04, S06, S08, S10, S12. Two groups in the table: F08, W06 with min product level 20 m below the antenna; H04, S06, S08, S10, S12 with 21 m below the antenna. Max product level is 1 m below the antenna for both.

The table can be extracted as a matrix table with antenna types. The model family could be the antennas — they're accessories/configurations rather than separate models. But the table varies by antenna type, so I could treat antenna type as model variants or config axis. The schema says config_level for attribute × config-axis matrix. The antennas are probably configurations of the same type XP. I'll model it as a config_level with axis "antenna_type" and also as matrix_tables.

Actually, let me think. "model Smartradar Flexline, type XP, with the antennas F08, W06, H04, S06, S08, S10 and S12" — the type is XP, and the antennas are accessories. The varying attribute is minimum product level. I'll use config_level:

```json
{
  "attribute": "minimum_product_level",
  "axis": "antenna_type",
  "values": [
    {"condition": "F08, W06", "value": -20, "unit_symbol": "m"},
    {"condition": "H04, S06, S08, S10, S12", "value": -21, "unit_symbol": "m"}
  ]
}
```

Hmm, the value is "20 m below the antenna" — negative could be confusing. Better keep value as string "20 m below the antenna"? Rules say numbers not strings, but "below the antenna" is a reference frame. Value 20 m below the antenna... I could set value as {min: null, max: -20}? No. The minimum product level is 20 m below the antenna, meaning the product level can be as low as 20 m below the antenna. So minimum = -20 m relative to antenna. Max = -1 m. That's a defensible interpretation, but might be over-interpretation. Safer to keep value as string "20 m below the antenna"? The rules prefer numbers. But reference-relative measurements... I think using string value "20 m below antenna" is acceptable since it's not purely numeric. Actually the rules say: "Formulas/symbols. When the value is a formula like Emax/14000 or a symbol like Emax, keep it as a string". Relative-to-antenna values are similar. Hmm.

Alternatively: minimum_product_level: value 20, unit "m", with a qualifier in the attribute or value. The instruction says pure structured. I'll go with:

{"condition": "F08, W06", "value": {"min": null, "max": -20}, "unit_symbol": "m"}? No, that inverts.

Let me just use value: -20 m for minimum product level (below antenna as negative reference) and -1 m for maximum product level. Actually that's clean and captures the physics. But risk of misinterpretation... The footnote/description can clarify. I could add attribute "minimum_product_level_below_antenna". Hmm, but then unit symbol "m" and value 20 with the attribute name conveying "below antenna". That's clear: minimum_product_level_below_antenna: 20 m; maximum_product_level_below_antenna: 1 m. That's clean and unambiguous. I'll do that.

Also accuracy class 2 per antenna group.

Characteristics type_level: accuracy_class: 2 (dimensionless). The R85 recommendation accuracy_classes: ["2"].

Matrix table:
```json
{
  "name": "Antenna types and product level limits",
  "columns": ["antenna_type", "accuracy_class", "minimum_product_level_below_antenna", "maximum_product_level_below_antenna"],
  "rows": [
    {"antenna_type": "F08, W06", "accuracy_class": 2, "minimum_product_level_below_antenna": 20, "maximum_product_level_below_antenna": 1},
    {"antenna_type": "H04, S06, S08, S10, S12", "accuracy_class": 2, "minimum_product_level_below_antenna": 21, "maximum_product_level_below_antenna": 1}
  ],
  "description": "..."
}
```

The liquid/vapour pressure/temperature columns say "The manufacturer shall specify these values for each application." — descriptive text, not values. I can include them in the matrix rows as strings or omit. I'll include in description.

Test reports: R85/1998-NL1-07.03, 100 pages, role type_evaluation_report (it says "associated Test Report"). Role: "test_report". The schema role options: type_evaluation_report | test_report | documentation_file | evaluation_report. It's called "Test Report" — use "test_report". Date not given. Pages 100.

Recommendation: id "R85", edition 1998 (int), accuracy_classes ["2"]. The edition is "1998 (E)" — edition 1998.

Scheme: The certificate scheme... scheme (A|B). This is an OIML Certificate of Conformity under the OIML-CS. R85/1998-NL1-07.03 — older cert, likely scheme A. Not stated explicitly. Hmm. The cert format looks like the older basic system. OIML-CS scheme A vs B: Scheme A certificates require test reports. This cert references a test report. Most NMi certs of this era... I think it's safer to omit scheme since not stated. But the schema asks for scheme (A|B). Many extractors would infer... I'll omit since not explicitly stated. Actually, hmm — let me think. The certificate includes "represented by the sample or samples identified in the associated Test Report" — both schemes include that. I'll omit scheme to avoid fabrication. Rule 8: don't fabricate. Omit.

Certificate number: "R85/1998-NL1-07.03". oiml_issuer_id: not given. Omit.

Revision history: none. Footnotes: none.

Page total: 2 (Page 1 of 2, Page 2 of 2).

date_issued: 2007-10-11.

Category: "Automatic level gauge" — from the schema examples, categories like "Load cell", "Indicator", "Measuring system"... R85 is "Automatic level gauges". I'll use "Automatic level gauge".

Model family: include only if cert covers >1 model variant. The antennas are variants of type XP. I think it's reasonable to include model_family with models per antenna: F08, W06, H04, S06, S08, S10, S12. Or the two groups. The varying attributes differ between the two groups. I could list all 7 antennas as model variants with attributes. That would be cleanest:

models: F08, W06, H04, S06, S08, S10, S12, each with attributes {minimum_product_level_below_antenna: 20 or 21, maximum_product_level_below_antenna: 1, accuracy_class: 2}.

And model_level characteristics:
- minimum_product_level_below_antenna: values per model (20 for F08/W06, 21 for others), unit m
- maximum_product_level_below_antenna: 1 m for all

And type_level: accuracy_class 2.

Also config_level as alternative? I'll use model_level since antennas are the variant dimension, plus the matrix table. Both are allowed.

type_designations: ["XP"] for the type; antennas are accessories. Should antennas go in type_designations? They're named identifiers, so include: ["XP", "F08", "W06", "H04", "S06", "S08", "S10", "S12"]. And Smartradar Flexline is the model/family name. model_family.family_name: "Smartradar Flexline".

module_designation: null / omit — not applicable; the certified type is a complete instrument (automatic level gauge). I'll set "Not applicable"? Rule: module_designation "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. Not stated in doc; I'll omit (null) to avoid fabrication.

Components: antennas could be components with role "antenna" and type designations, alternatives "OR". That seems appropriate: cert names sub-assemblies (antennas). I'll add:

```json
{
  "role": "antenna",
  "type_designations": ["F08", "W06", "H04", "S06", "S08", "S10", "S12"],
  "alternatives": "OR"
}
```

Characteristics for the components: the level ranges could attach to antenna types. I'll keep them at model_level.

Issuing authority address_lines: ["Hugo de Grootplein 1", "3314 EG Dordrecht", "The Netherlands"]. There's also P.O. Box in the footer — that's the footer of NMi Certin; the authority address block says Hugo de Grootplein 1. I'll use the main address; could include P.O. Box too. I'll keep the primary block.

Person title: "Manager Product Certification".

Phone: "+31 78 6332332". Fax: schema doesn't list fax; skip or include? Schema fields: phone, email, website. Skip fax.

Scheme A|B: omit.

Let me also consider oiml_issuer_id — some certs have "NMi Certin" notification number. Not present. Omit.
